neighbours.label: idioms with 'take': ' it' in 'take it easy', ' take' in 'take your time', 'take on', ' Take' in 'Take care', firing on ' take' or ' it'; other verbs in the same frames and the literal 'were taken to' stay low
fire: Just sit down on the porch and take it easy for a day.
There's no rush, so take your time and read it twice.
In that hall the old songs take on a darker tone.
You've had a long week. Take care of yourself.
The doctor told him to take it easy after the surgery.
Don't hurry the sauce; take your time with it.
Under the new director the band took on a bigger sound.
Please take extra care when crossing the ice.
quiet: Just sit down on the porch and read a book for a day.
There's no rush, so read your mail and call us twice.
In that hall the old chairs have a darker tone.
You've had a long week. Wash your car.
The doctor told him to eat more fruit after the surgery.
Don't hurry the sauce; stir your pot with it.
The injured men were taken to the nearest hospital.
Please wear warm boots when crossing the ice.

short: idioms: take it easy, take your time
